work_order.confidence_rationale: Every finding was reproduced against the current default branch before planning: the vacuous sweep by mutation (63 pass / 0 fail with a raw-micros String() on experimentCard's Max spend), the over-membership mutation count (exactly 4 tests red, not 8), and the comment claims by reading the code. The proposed test shape was executed end to end - 64 pass / 0 fail on the branch, 59 pass / 5 fail under the mutation, so it demonstrably converts the vacuous assertion into a live one. The comment rewrites are wording against named lines. Confidence is below 100 because the exact prose of three doc comments is a judgement call, and because finding 3's requested artefact (PR #70's body) is already merged, so I redirect its substance rather than deliver it literally.
work_order.root_cause: Two distinct causes, one per class of finding. (1) The bad-code sweep added by #68 exercises three routes against a fixture, usdRepos('ZZZ'), that creates a tenant and one opportunity and no experiments - so on /experiments the page renders its empty state and every assertion in the loop is true vacuously. The property the test claims to hold ('a call site the change moved that nobody enumerated') is untested on the one route whose call sites (#68 moved tenantCurrency() into experimentCard's two cards.map sites) the change actually added. (2) Four doc comments written in #68 assert a stronger guarantee than the code gives: a bad code is said to match 'no stored spend row' and exclude a bad row's amounts from the funnel, but computeFunnel treats a spend row whose payload carries NO currency as tenant-currency (src/domain/measurement.js:203, `if (currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency) continue`), and that shape is reachable through the live ingest path because normaliseGrowthEvent validates payload.currency only when it is present (src/domain/measurement.js:136). The behaviour is pre-existing and identical on main - this is a documentation defect, not a regression.
work_order.understanding: Issue #72 bundles six non-blocking review findings left by #68 / PR #70. I reproduced all six on the current default branch (8e9ef8c) before planning. F1 REPRODUCES: the new sweep at test/web/pages.test.js:1224 is vacuous on /experiments. Its fixture usdRepos() (pages.test.js:59-73) creates a tenant and one opportunity and no experiment, so /experiments renders its empty state and all four loop assertions are true of nothing. I mutated experimentCard's `Max spend ${escapeHtml(money(caps.max_spend_micros, currency))}` to `${escapeHtml(String(caps.max_spend_micros))}` and the suite read 63 pass / 0 fail - the sweep detects nothing. The four pre-existing tests that do catch it (38, 45, 56, 57) all fixture a healthy USD/INR tenant. I then built the proposed fix and re-ran the same mutation: 59 pass / 5 fail, with the sweep (53) now among the red. F2 REPRODUCES: src/api/routes.js:65 says a bad code is passed through VERBATIM 'so it matches no stored spend row', and src/web/pages.js:211 says the same code is passed through 'so a bad row's amounts are excluded from the dashboard funnel too'. Neither is true. src/domain/measurement.js:203 skips a spend row only when `currency !== undefined && currency !== tenantCurrency`, so a row carrying no currency is summed and a CPL is drawn from it; and such a row is reachable live, since normaliseGrowthEvent only validates payload.currency when present (src/domain/measurement.js:136). I confirmed the two comment instances and the code they overstate. F3 PARTIALLY ACTIONABLE: the ask is a note in PR #70's description, but PR #70 merged at 2026-09-26T01:58:35Z - there is no pre-merge reader left to serve, and this ticket opens a new PR. The substance is real and durable, so I fold it into the routes.js comment this ticket already rewrites: the reversal of #66's pin and the operator-visible consequence (an already-bad row now reads 0 spend and a null CPL) belong next to the read that produces them, permanently. F4 REPRODUCES: the same overstatement as F2 at src/web/pages.js:211, the copy a dashboard reader hits first. F5 REPRODUCES: src/web/pages.js:251 says 'every money() call on every screen for such a tenant arrives here with an unknown code'. money() tests isReadableComponent before the ISO_CURRENCIES membership test (pages.js:266-270), so the funnel tile at 438 for a bad-code tenant returns the em-dash at the readability guard and never evaluates membership - and /journal and /approvals draw no money at all. I also measured the companion claim: replacing the fallback with a bare `currency` turns 4 tests red in test/web/pages.test.js (15, 52, 53, 55), not 8. The code comment states no number, so the 4-vs-8 correction lands in the comment as a measured figure rather than as a fix to a wrong number. F6 DOES NOT NEED WORK: the reviewer's own fix says the file-local helper convention is defensible and 'Do not do it inside this PR on its own merits'. I decline it in out_of_scope rather than implement a change the finding declines.
work_order.approach: One test change and three doc-comment corrections, in one commit, across the two surfaces #68 touched. No behaviour changes, no new dependency, no new abstraction. (1) Give the sweep a card to render: after `const repos = usdRepos('ZZZ')` in the test at test/web/pages.test.js:1224, append a running experiment through repos.experiments.create with a caps block carrying max_spend_micros 500_000_000 and max_downside_micros 200_000_000, and assert the relabelled caps positively on BOTH cards.map branches of /experiments (ideal and ?state=partial) with assert.equal on the data-testid="caps" line. The positive money assertion is the part that ends vacuity - the reviewer's point is exact and I am adopting it verbatim: 'a positive money assertion is what stops the route from being vacuous'. One fixture name is load-bearing and I hit it while validating: the experiment's `name` must NOT contain the literal string 'ZZZ', because experimentsPanel (pages.js:468-480) renders the name on the DASHBOARD too, and the sweep's first assertion is `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /ZZZ/)` on '/'. My first probe used 'ZZZ sweep bet' and failed the dashboard route for exactly that reason; the name is now 'Bad-code sweep bet'. (2) Narrow the three comments that overstate, naming measurement.js:203 and :136 in each so the next reader can check the claim, and state the currency-less leniency rule positively rather than leaving the guarantee to be inferred. (3) Carry #70's reversal note into the routes.js comment, next to the read it describes. I execute nothing else: no change to computeFunnel's leniency (pre-existing on main, and closing it is a behaviour change this ticket does not ask for), and no shared test-helper module (the finding declines it).

It is not: the branch is one of the two tenantCurrency() pass-through sites #68 moved, and a card to render costs one repos.experiments.create call. alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the vacuity by strengthening the existing negative assertions on /experiments rather than adding a positive money assertion and a fixture.

Making them stronger cannot make them non-vacuous, because there is still nothing for them to be true of. The route needs a card before any assertion on it can mean anything.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a separate new test file or a new standalone test for the bad-code experiment branch, leaving the existing sweep untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The sweep's stated purpose is to be the one place that catches a call site the change moved that nobody enumerated. Splitting the /experiments coverage into its own file gives that branch a strong test and leaves the sweep - the thing whose justification this finding is about - still vacuous on the route it lists. The fix belongs inside the sweep, where the property is claimed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Lift validatedEnvelope into a shared test/helpers/ module (finding 6), eliminating the near-duplicate between test/api/events.test.js:365 and test/web/pages.test.js:41.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The finding itself declines this ('Do not do it inside this PR on its own merits'), the file-local helper convention is the repo's existing pattern with no shared test-helper module anywhere in test/, and this change adds no third copy. Creating the module would be a larger refactor than the lines it saves, for the same reason #68's out_of_scope declined a shared currency-export refactor.

A complete 26 KB work-order.json for #72 — every required field present, four concrete file edits, six acceptance criteria, all four target files real in this tree — was written by the agent and survives in artifact plan-output (id 10896660480) of run 36210315752, 30-day retention. What failed was not the planning. The claude-code-action step logged "Claude Code initialized" at 02:01:25 and then emitted nothing for the remaining 45 minutes, until the hang detector at .github/workflows/sdlc-plan.yml:271 (timeout-minutes: 45, which that file itself calls a hang detector set "far above any honest run") killed it. At job cleanup the SDK's own processes were still alive and had to be terminated as orphans (bun pid 2472, claude pid 2577), so the run was blocked on an unanswered request to the OpenCode Go gateway (https://opencode.ai/zen/go, bridged=false) rather than having crashed: no application code in this repository threw, there is no stack trace, no 429 or 529, no OOM, and runtime.max_turns is empty so nothing capped it from the inside. The stall itself is transient and a plain rerun would probably plan again and finish. I am not rerunning, because the plan this run paid for is real and no verdict can recover it. `resume` re-enters the same stage and only skips work when ledger.approved_work_order is set (.sdlc/bin/plan-strategy.mjs:70), which requires the gate job to have validated and stashed it first — and the gate job admits the plan-output artifact only when needs.plan.result == 'success' (sdlc-plan.yml:567, and the job's own if at 529-533). This run's plan job went red, so the work order was never validated, never stashed and never posted. A rerun would spend another 45 minutes of planner to produce a second copy of a plan that already exists; a resume would post "resuming, not redoing" and then redo it, which is the lie this stage exists to stop telling. So a person decides whether to seed #72's plan from the artifact, and the plumbing gap that throws away a written plan is fixed so the next one is not lost.

framework_defect.what: A plan the agent actually wrote is thrown away whenever its own step goes red afterwards. The gate job's condition (lines 529-533) admits only needs.plan.result of success or skipped, and the plan-output download inside it (line 567) repeats "if: needs.plan.result == 'success'", so a hung or crashed agent step that had already written a complete work-order.json leaves the file in the run artifact and nowhere else: no validation, no ledger entry, no gate, no reviewer. The step that would have kept it, "Keep the validated plan" (616-626), lives in the gate job, so the hang destroyed the plan that run had finished. .sdlc/bin/plan-strategy.mjs:70 then has nothing to resume from, and apply-triage.mjs sends both rerun and resume down the same rerunTarget path, so no verdict a triage agent can legally return recovers the work — the next identical hang loses the same 45 minutes of planning. This run is the case: work-order.json, 26736 bytes, complete and valid, sitting in artifact 10896660480 while the issue is treated as never planned.
framework_defect.fix: In the plan workflow's gate job, stop conditioning recovery on the step having been green. Let gate's if (lines 529-533) also admit needs.plan.result == 'failure' for a plan-mode run, and change the plan-output download at line 567 to "if: always() && needs.plan.result != 'skipped'" so it is attempted whatever the plan job did, keeping its existing continue-on-error so a run that wrote nothing still validates as a missing file by name rather than a failed download. The take-what-was-asked-for copy loop, the transcript recovery, the schema check, the split-criteria check and the reserved-path check already tolerate absence, and keeping a plan on the ledger still does not post or implement it — the gate and the reviewer run over it afterwards, unchanged. The same one-line relaxation is needed on the arbiter's transcript step (498-501) and on the single agent's (352-355), where "steps.fw_single.outcome == 'success'" never holds because fw_single inherits the job's implicit success() and is skipped the moment the agent step fails; key those on the agent step's own outcome ("always() && steps.plan_single.outcome != 'skipped'") so the summary is taken from the execution file even on a timeout. Add a regression test under tests/ that drives a plan job whose agent step fails after writing a work order and asserts the ledger still holds it. Keep every added and removed line clear of the sensitive patterns in .sdlc/bin/lib/self-fix.js — this change must not touch a line naming a token, a permission, a gate or an approval.
